                                        Summary

               If the origin of the moving coordinate system is chosen at the center of mass of a rigid body, then its kinetic
          energy splits into the kinetic energies of translational and rotational motion:

                                                1       1
                                     T =  µV2 +  IikΩiΩk
                                                2       2

         where M is the total mass of the body, V is the velocity of the center of mass, Ijk = X m(xixiδij −xjxk)
              is the central tensor of inertia, Ωi are the components of the angular velocity vector projected onto the axes
           of the moving coordinate system, xk are coordinates of a point in moving coordinate system
        The diagonal elements of the inertia tensor, namely I11, I22, I33, are referred to as the axial moments of
            inertia, as they coincide with the moments of inertia of the rigid body about the moving coordinate axes
          x1, x2, x3, respectively.
        The principal axes of inertia are defined as those moving axes (with their origin at the center of mass) in
         which the inertia tensor is diagonal. In this case, the diagonal components of the inertia tensor are called the
           principal moments of inertia and are denoted by I1, I2, I3.
